Load Patient Plan
The steps for loading a patient plan depend on your system configuration.
If your system does not have networked login or the Intuitive Network Drive configured, proceed to USB Only on page 68.
If the Intuitive Network Drive is configured on your system, proceed to USB or Network Drive on page 69.
Note: Information for the patient plan selection includes patient name, medical record number (MRN), and plan date.
USB Only
To load a patient plan:
1. Insert the USB storage device with the exported patient plan into the USB input on the Controller.
2. Select the patient plan on the Controller touchscreen.
3. Check the details of the patient plan and ID, and then tap Confirm to load the plan.

To change patient plans at any point, select the Menu icon > Patient Plans and select a new plan. If a plan is updated mid-procedure, ensure that the correct plan is selected after re-inserting the USB device into the Controller.
USB or Network Drive
If your system has access to the Network Drive, you can load a plan onto the system from the Network Drive or from a USB device.

Note: Before you can access plans on the Network Drive, you must complete a one-time linking process between your Intuitive account and your local PlanPoint account. For instructions on linking your accounts, see the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
Note: If you load a plan from the Network Drive, a USB device is still required to collect screenshots and video recording during a procedure.
1. If loading a plan from the Network Drive:
a. Ensure you have logged in to your Intuitive account (see 8.5 Log in to Your Intuitive Account on page 67).
b. Enter your six-digit Intuitive PIN to authenticate your account.
If needed, open the PIN pad by tapping the Menu icon > Patient Plans . Tap the Network tab, then tap the Enter PIN button.
Note: If you cannot access the Network Drive, load the patient plan onto the system using a USB device and contact Customer Service.
2. If loading a plan from a USB device:
a. Ensure you have logged in to your Intuitive account if you wish to collect real-time case data associated with your procedure (see 8.5 Log in to Your Intuitive Account on page 67).
b. If prompted for your PIN, you may tap Skip on the PIN pad to bypass authentication. Authentication is required only to access patient plans on the Network Drive.
c. Insert the USB device with the exported plan into the USB input on the Controller.
3. Select the patient plan from either the USB or the Network tab. If needed, navigate to the tabs by tapping the Menu icon > Patient Plans .
Note: If you are loading the plan from the Network Drive and the plan is not available, load the plan onto the system using a USB device.
4. Tap Continue on the confirmation window to confirm your selection.

To change plans at any point, tap the Menu icon > Patient Plans and select a new plan. If a plan is updated mid-procedure, re-export the plan to the USB or Network Drive and select the correct plan on the system.
Note
Preview Plan
Once the patient plan loads onto the system, you may preview the plan prior to registration.

Tap Preview Path on the Controller touchscreen to preview the path. Press and hold the forward or backward arrow icons on the Controller touchscreen side panel to move the preview path view along the pathway. To exit, tap x. It is recommended that the patient be placed in the supine position, with the head at the edge of the bed and with the neck slightly extended to expose the glottic plane.
Physician discretion on patient positioning is advised.
2. Administer anesthesia.

3. Intubate the patient with ET tube. Confirm that the distal end of the ET tube is approximately 2 to 5 cm proximal to the main carina. After the patient is intubated and under general anesthesia, secure the ET tube to the patient's head to prevent extubation.
4. Verify ET tube placement using a standard bronchoscope. Ensure minimal bends in the ET tube to facilitate smooth passage of the Catheter through the trachea.
5. Position the fluoro device to be used later in the procedure.
6. Connect the Swivel Connector to the ET tube after patient intubation.
7. Connect the anesthesia tubes to the Swivel Connector.
Survey Airway: It is optional to insert a standard bronchoscope for manual survey of the airway. When finished, remove the standard bronchoscope.
Dock to Patient
WARNING: When docking to patient, always stabilize the endotracheal tube (ET tube). While docked, always release tension before adjusting ET tube as this may result in loss of ventilation.
WARNING: Do not move patient bed after docking the system to the patient. Moving the patient bed may result in loss of ventilation pathway.
WARNING:
To avoid patient injury, always lock the wheels of the System Cart before docking to the patient.
Follow the on-screen prompts to dock to the patient. The system is now ready for procedure and biopsy.
End of Section
Register

WARNING: To prevent impaired ventilation and patient injury, the procedure should be performed under general anesthesia with endotracheal intubation, Electrocardiography (ECG) monitoring, and ventilator alarms.

Registration is the process used to match the airway Live View with the Navigation View. During registration, the system collects apical and basal data for each lung. These apical and basal segments are displayed on the system as four quadrants, which are regional divisions of the Airway Tree (that is, the quadrants are not anatomically divided by lobe).

Follow the steps on the top monitor to perform airway registration. Note: Use Show Lung Regions to display the separation of the lung into the four quadrants with their associated colors on the Airway Tree (note that these quadrants are not based on lobes).

If the system checks the wrong quadrant, continue to drive to all four apical and basal regions of the lung. If quadrant checks are missing after you have navigated to all four regions, proceed with partial registration. It is not recommended to continue navigating to get all four quadrant checks if apical and basal data has been gathered. To evaluate registration, navigate beyond the main carina and evaluate the relationship between the Live View and the Navigation View, especially at carinas proximal to the region of interest. Some discrepancy may occur due to biological motion.
Redo registration if there is a visual mismatch between the Live View and Navigation View during navigation, or if there is significant patient or system movement.
Redo registration if the Swivel Connector is undocked from the arm, the arm clutch button is pressed, the System Cart brakes are unlocked, or the Catheter is removed from the system mid-procedure.
Ion System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual 553990-11 Rev. C
Navigate

After registration is complete, the first planned destination (target and path) automatically appears on screen. The planned pathway to the target appears on the Navigation View, Tree View, and Progress View. It is possible to switch to an alternate target or pathway if one was planned.
Navigation of the Catheter through the airways should be performed in a minimally traumatic manner by attempting to stay in the center of the airways at all times.
WARNING: Advance the Catheter only under live visualization from the Vision Probe (Live View) to prevent procedural delay or patient injury.
WARNING: Do not activate the scroll wheel while interacting with the Controller touchscreen, as this may result in pneumothorax.
Note: Navigation View should be used as guidance only.
Note:
The Swivel Connector may partially disconnect from the arm due to Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter.
To navigate to the target and position the Catheter for biopsy:
1. Use the Controller to drive the Catheter through the planned pathway to the target. Watch the Live View while driving.

2. Once the target is reached, note the message to use fluoroscopic guidance when extending tools past the tip of the Catheter. Using Navigation View for reference, aim the Catheter as straight as possible toward the center of the target.
Ensure the target is within striking distance of the needle (approximately 30 mm).
For endoluminal targets: Position the Catheter tip directly against the target.

For extra bronchial targets: Position the Catheter tip against the airway wall for stability. If needed, pull the Vision Probe back slightly to visually confirm that the Catheter tip sits directly against the airway wall.
5. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and keep the Vision Probe out of the way by placing it into the Vision Probe bag.
6. For biopsy, adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.
Biopsy Overview
WARNING: To prevent patient injury, do not use excessive force during the insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel.

WARNING: When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly releaxes in response to the fault.
Note:

Vibrations from insertion or extraction of the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools through the Catheter tool channel may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
Before Biopsy
Ensure that the fluoroscope or other third-party visualization sources are connected to the System Cart and are functional.
Before Tool Exchange
Before inserting or removing any tool through the Catheter tool channel, check the Bend Radius on the monitor to ensure there is sufficient space to pass the tool through the Catheter tip.

Whereas the Progress View indicates the Catheter bends along the shaft, the Tip Indicator shows the direction the Catheter tip is bent, and the Bend Radius shows the tightest bend on the Catheter (measured in millimeters).
The bend radius must be large enough when passing the following tools:
Flexision Biopsy Needle: 15 mm or greater
Third-party tools: 20 mm or greater
Forceps: 25 mm or greater
For guidance selecting compatible third-party tools, see the third-party tools table in 8.2 Select Compatible Third-Party Biopsy Tools on page 58.
If needed, relax the Catheter before passing a tool as follows:

1. (Optional) Before entering the passive state, place a biopsy marker to mark your biopsy position. After passing the tool, you can return to active mode and re-articulate to the biopsy marker to return to your parked position.
2. Relax the Catheter using either method:
Articulate the Catheter toward the white arrow on the tip indicator to increase the bend radius.
Press the Passive button on the Controller to put the Catheter in passive (relaxed) mode.
Pass the tool.

CAUTION: If resistance is felt when removing the Vision Probe or tool from the Catheter tool channel, do not continue retracting the device, as this may result in device damage. Remove the Catheter and Vision Probe or tool together.
4. If needed, press the Passive button again to return to active mode.
5. Re-articulate the Catheter to your biopsy position.
After Biopsy Always Evaluate Airway
WARNING: Insert the Vision Probe after biopsy to assess airways for trauma or bleeding to prevent delayed intervention in case of an emergency.
After a biopsy, insert the Vision Probe back in the Catheter to check for bleeding, and to inspect the Catheter liner for damage. If the liner is damaged, replace the Catheter.
Ion System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual 553990-11 Rev. C
Flexision Needle Biopsy
WARNING: Always inspect the biopsy needle for damage before and during use. A damaged needle can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.
WARNING: Use fluoroscopic visualization (fluoroscopy) when advancing tools past the tip of the Catheter. Failure to use fluoroscopy during biopsy may result in patient injury.

WARNING: Always reset the needle stop (re-sheath the needle): before removing the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel, after preparing the sample, or before transferring the needle between staff. Failure to reset the needle stop during handling or hand-offs may result in infection or injury by needle stick.
WARNING: If you notice damage to the inside of the Catheter during use, replace the Catheter. A damaged Catheter can contain loose fragments that may cause toxic reaction if left in the patient.

CAUTION: Proceed with caution if the biopsy needle is inserted or removed through a Catheter bend radius smaller than 15 mm. Insertion and removal of the biopsy needle should not be performed against increased resistance. Failure to follow instructions may result in Catheter or needle damage.
CAUTION:
Exercise caution when inserting the biopsy needle into the Catheter tool channel with the sheath extended. Failure to do so may result in patient injury.
1. Inspect the biopsy needle prior to use. If damaged, dispose and replace the needle.
a. Before use of the needle, confirm the label is legible and is the intended needle size.
b. Before use and between each use, inspect the needle for the following:
Damage to sheath shaft, sheath tip, needle tube, and needle point (for example, burrs or dull edges at needle point, loose or separated needle, or kinks).
Foreign matter.
Friction when extending needle, or inability to fully extend needle (approximately 3 cm).
Blocked or kinked lumen. Check by flushing with saline.
Ensure needle stop is functioning properly. Proper function is described as:
When the needle stop is pressed, the needle stop should slide freely.
When the needle stop is released, the needle stop should be locked.
Stylet does not extend beyond the tip of the needle (more than 3 mm).

c. Before inserting or reinserting into the Catheter tool channel, confirm the needle is fully retracted and locked within the sheath, the needle sheath home position mark is fully exposed, and the thumbscrew has locked the sheath extension. WARNING: Confirm the relation of the patient anatomy to the biopsy target (for example, distances to target and anatomy borders) before setting needle stroke length. Setting the incorrect needle stroke length may lead to pneumothorax.
4. While stabilizing the needle handle, set the needle insertion depth using the needle stop up to 3 cm based on the distance to the target and size of the target.

The insertion distance should be based on physician discretion. The estimated distance of the Catheter to the target is shown on the monitor. Consider minimum distance to target as provided by the navigation, sheath extension, and fluoroscopy before choosing a needle extension length.
5. Under fluoroscopy, insert the needle with one jab towards the target.
If needed, check the recommended fluoro arm angle on the monitor and adjust the fluoro arm.
6. Once the needle is inserted, remove the stylet from the back end of the needle while holding the needle in place.

At the physician's discretion, suction can be attached to the needle. For suction, connect the stopcock to the vacuum syringe provided with the needle. With the stopcock closed, pull back vacuum for 5 to 20 mL. Connect the stopcock to the needle and open the valve towards the needle.
Note: Select a vacuum locking syringe and stopcock with standard luer lock connectors (luer fittings compliant with ISO 80369-7) that can suction up to 20 mL.
7. Perform multiple jabs with the needle, per physician discretion.
8. Remove the vacuum syringe and, under fluoroscopy, fully retract the needle into the sheath, and return the needle stop to the home position.

9. If desired, fully retract the sheath and tighten the thumbscrew. If you opt to keep the sheath extended for further passes, exercise caution when re-inserting the needle into the Catheter tool channel.
10. Press the connector key and pull the biopsy needle from the Catheter tool channel.
11. Evaluate airway.
Perform airway evaluation after all the biopsy passes are complete. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for any bleeding.
Remove Samples
1. Take the biopsy needle to the back table for retrieving samples.
a. Set the needle insertion limit.
b. With the sheath pointing towards the sample tray, advance the needle.
c. Push the sample out using a syringe filled with air.
The sample can also be pushed out using the stylet, if the sample is stuck in the needle.
2. Use a syringe to inject saline in the needle to collect the remaining sample.
a. Retract the needle and secure the needle stop.
b. Reinsert the stylet into the needle and lock in place. Ensure the needle is not damaged (for example, bent or broken).
Repeat Needle Biopsy
1. To repeat biopsy, insert the needle and repeat the needle biopsy steps to perform another biopsy pass from the same target to collect an appropriate sample size, at the physician's discretion.
2. Perform biopsy passes.
At the physician's discretion, use the biopsy marker feature to indicate multiple biopsy attempts. Use the trackball to articulate to another area of the target to take another biopsy.

Use the orientation guide on the bottom monitor to determine how to move the trackball for the desired Catheter tip articulation. Move the trackball to the right, left, up, or down like a clock. For example, in the image below, to articulate the Catheter tip in the cranial direction, move the trackball towards 7 o'clock.

The Endoluminal Compass is a fixed sphere with directional indicators that display in the Navigation View around the orientation guide. The directional indicators represent anatomical headings that are determined by the pre-procedure CT scan. The Endoluminal Compass is set to visible by default.
Medial and lateral indicators on the Endoluminal Compass and the orientation guide change based on the location of the Catheter.
3. Remove samples from the needle (see Remove Samples on page 82).
Note:
The rotational orientation of third-party tools is not controlled through the Catheter tool channel. Rotation may affect insertion and retraction through the Catheter.
1. Insert compatible third-party tools through the Catheter tool channel.
a. Ensure that the Catheter bend radius is greater than 25 mm if inserting forceps or greater than 20 mm if inserting any other third-party tools.
b. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.
2. Deploy the tool to retrieve the sample of the target tissue under fluoroscopy.
3. Remove the tool and evaluate the airway. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter to evaluate the biopsy site for bleeding.
Forceps
WARNING: Failure to properly insert or remove forceps through the Catheter tool channel may damage the forceps, resulting in procedure delay or foreign body in the patient.
1. Press the Passive
a. Ensure the forceps are fully closed.
Note:
The Catheter must be in passive mode prior to retracting biopsy forceps.

Note: Slowly insert and retract biopsy forceps through the Catheter tool channel. Quickly inserting and retracting may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
1. Press the Passive button on the Controller, and carefully retract through the Catheter.
If resistance is felt while retracting forceps, confirm the Catheter is in passive mode. If resistance is still felt consider the following: a. Ensure the forceps are fully closed.
b. Gently rotate the forceps back and forth while retracting until the resistance is overcome. If resistance persists, or the tool is jammed, remove the Catheter and biopsy tool together.

Ion System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual 553990-11 Rev. C Syringe WARNING: Always wear personal protective equipment when removing the Vision Probe, biopsy needle, or bronchoscopic tools from the Catheter tool channel after saline injection. Failure to do so may result in infection if saline regurgitation occurs while removing these items.
CAUTION: Exercise caution if injecting air through the Catheter when the Catheter is in the peripheral airways. Injecting air when the Catheter is wedged in small airways may result in patient harm.
CAUTION: Suction excess fluid injected during broncheoalveolar lavage (BAL), as excess fluid may impair lung function.
1. Use a 20 mL locking syringe to infuse warmed saline (room temperature) through the Catheter tool channel into the airways.
2. Apply suction with the syringe to withdraw the administered saline rinse into the syringe.
Third-Party Bronchoalveolar Lavage Kit
Note: When possible before performing lavage, it is recommended to retract the Catheter so it is away from the airway walls for free fluid flow.
1. Connect the tubing of the bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) container to the narrowed, ribbed portion of the Suction Adapter.
2. Connect the wall suction tubing to the BAL container.
3. Infuse saline with a 20 mL syringe through the Catheter tool channel into the airways.
4. Connect the Suction Adapter, with the BAL container attached, onto the Catheter tool channel.
CAUTION: Do not apply suction for extended durations, as this may impair ventilation or lead to procedure delay.

To collect sample into BAL container, apply gentle suction by closing the hole on the suction adapter. Modulate suction strength by partially closing the hole on the suction adapter, or by varying pressure.
6. Disconnect the BAL container from the Catheter and remove from wall suction once sample has been retrieved.

page_map.text: 6. Remove the brush from the Catheter.
Bronchial Balloons (Endobronchial Blockers)
At the physician's discretion, a blocking balloon may be entered through the Catheter.
1. Insert blocking balloon to desired location.
2. Using fluoroscopic visualization, fill balloon with a mix of saline and legally marketed contrast so it is visible on the fluoroscope.
3. Leave balloon in place as needed.
Repeat Navigation and Biopsy
1. Navigate to a second target (if applicable).
2. Repeat Navigation and Biopsy steps of the procedure.
Take Down System

Finish the procedure, and then clean, stow, shut down, and store the system as described in the next chapter. e. Remove the Catheter Guide from the arm using the release buttons on the Catheter Guide.
End of Section
Instrument and Accessory Uses

When instruments and accessories expire, they can no longer be used. Expired instruments, accessories, and any of their components must be properly disposed of following all applicable national and local laws and guidelines.
To view the number of instrument and accessory uses that remain, tap Menu > Accessory Uses on the Controller touchscreen, or view the Accessory Uses panel on the bottom monitor.
Clean and Disinfect System
Before stowing, follow on-screen guidance to wipe down the System Cart arm and Controller, for visual cleanliness. Clean the rest of the system in accordance with hospital or facility policies.
WARNING: Clean and disinfect both the Controller and System Cart arm after each procedure to prevent cross-contamination that may result in infection.
CAUTION:
Do not use these disinfectants on the System Cart or Controller:
CaviWipes1 (manufactured by Metrex)
Sani-Cloth AF3 (manufactured by PDI)
Continued use in the presence of cracks may lead to system damage including fluid intrusion and system errors. Contact Customer Service if any cracking is observed.
CAUTION: Do not spray liquids while disinfecting the Ion system. Use only pre-moistened wipes to clean the system. Cleaning with spraying liquids may result in system damage.
Note: Do not manually force the carriage to move unless necessary. Use carriage clutch button or scroll wheel to safely move the carriage.
Stow and Shut Down System

To help prevent collision while transporting the system, properly stow the system cart arm and monitors before shutting the system down. Once the system is shut down, the arm clutch button is inactivated. In an emergency, you can still adjust the arm manually. Fold the top monitor over the bottom monitor and compact the monitor arm as much as possible over the cart base.

Ion System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual 553990-11 Rev. C 5. Shut down the system by pressing and holding the System Cart Power button for at least three seconds or until the button blinks yellow (the Power button blinks yellow during shutdown).
If the Power button is unresponsive, press and hold the Power button until the system shuts down. If the issue persists, contact Customer Service.
Auto Stow Troubleshooting
If you cannot compress the arm with the Auto Stow button, you can compress the arm manually, even when the system prompts you to proceed with the automated workflow.
To compress the arm manually, 1. Press and hold the powered elevation button to bring the arm to a vertical position.
2. Press and hold the carriage clutch button to compress the arm to its minimal length.
3. Press and hold the arm clutch button to compact the arm and setup joint as much as possible over the cart base.
Proceed to
Step 4 on page 91 to continue stowing the system.
Store System
1. Transport the System Cart and Controller to storage.
2. Plug in the System Cart during storage.
Note: Do not store the system in a temperature below -20 ºC or higher than 60 ºC. Exposure to temperature outside the range -20 ºC to 60 °C may damage the product.
Ensure the storage room for the System Cart and the Controller meets the following specifications:
a. Room temperature between 50 to 86 °F (10 to 30 °C).
b. Relative humidity between 10 to 85% non-condensing.

3. Connect the Ethernet cable to the back of the System Cart and an existing hospital network (wall plate). This establishes OnSite connection and enables data transfer during storage. You do not need to power on the system to connect to OnSite.
End of Section 4. Use the arm clutch button with one hand, and gently pull the Swivel Connector with the other hand to undock the arm and move it out of the way.
A.2 Mid-procedure Restart

When you restart the system during a procedure, the system preserves your patient plan, registration, target and path selection, and any biopsy markers. The system does not preserve updates to the target and will log out of your Intuitive account if you were previously logged in.
To restart the system during a procedure:
1. If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and remove it from the Catheter.

2. Keep the Catheter attached to the arm (the Catheter shaft may remain inside the patient). If the Catheter is removed from the arm, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
3. Keep the system docked to the patient. If the system is undocked, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
If available, tap

Restart System on the Controller touchscreen followed by Restart System. Alternatively, you can restart the system manually with the System Cart Power button (press and hold the Power button for three seconds to power off the system; when the system is powered off, press the button again to power the system back on).
Note: Do not unlock the System Cart brakes or move the arm (setup joint) while the system restarts, or else you will be prompted to re-register after completing Guided Setup.
5. When the system powers back on, tap Start Catheter Check if available on the Controller touchscreen.
If the Start Catheter Check button is not available, skip Step 6 and follow the instructions on the monitors to complete Guided Setup and re-register.
If the Catheter check fails, skip Step 6 and follow the instructions on the monitors to reattach the Catheter, complete Guided Setup, and re-register.
6. After the Catheter check completes, compare Live View and Navigation View to assess registration.
To accept registration, tap Continue on the Controller touchscreen.
To re-do registration, tap Redo Registration on the Controller touchscreen.
A.3 Unexpected System Motion

Note: If the biopsy needle or a biopsy tool is advanced into the tissue through the Catheter tool channel, then pull the needle back into its protecting sheath and into the Catheter before pressing E-stop.

If the system behaves in an unexpected manner that could harm the patient: Pressing the E-stop button locks all arm buttons, joints, and brakes. Use force against the arm to move it out of the way if necessary.

2. Once E-stop is pressed, the Catheter will slowly transition into Passive mode. At this time the user can uninstall the Catheter from the arm and manually pull back the Catheter gently from the patient. Proceed with undocking the Swivel Connector from the System Cart.
A.4 Mid-Procedure System Cart or Bed Height Adjustment WARNING: Do not move patient bed after docking the system to the patient. Moving the patient bed may result in loss of ventilation pathway.
If the System Cart or bed height needs adjustment mid-procedure, undock the system before any adjustment.
1. If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced into tissue through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and then into the Catheter.
2. Retract the Catheter using scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
3. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
4. Use the arm clutch button with one hand, and gently pull the Swivel Connector with the other hand to undock the arm and move it out of the way.
Adjust System Cart or bed height as needed.
6. Once adjustments are made, re-dock the system, insert the lubricated Catheter back into the ET tube, extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
7. Perform registration again.
A.5 Unable to Complete Registration

If the survey for one or both of the main bronchi cannot be completed, tap Proceed with Partial Survey on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial survey and continue to the next step of registration.

If the survey for one or more of the regions cannot be completed, use the Show Lung Regions feature to assist in identifying airways in that region. Then, tap Proceed with Partial Registration on the Controller touchscreen to accept the partial registration and continue to the final step of registration.
Note: You will need to register 4 cm on each side of the main carina to complete registration.
A.6 Registration with Variant Anatomy

If the patient has had a previous resection, use Show Lung Regions to view the corresponding quadrant assignments on the top monitor. Use these quadrant assignments as a guide during registration. If the main carina point is not situated at the anatomical main carina (for example, due to a pneumonectomy), still navigate to this main carina point and begin registration from there. Again, use Show Lung Regions to assist with registration.
If you are unable to complete the quadrant survey, ensure that apical and basal regions of the lung are registered and proceed with partial registration.
If needed, you can review the plan on the Planning Laptop to perform further troubleshooting. See the troubleshooting information in the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.

A.8 USB Errors
Error Reading USB
The system cannot read the USB. Try re-inserting the USB. If the issue persists, use a different USB drive.

Note: If a plan has already been loaded when you get this error, you may continue with the loaded plan, but note that you cannot take screenshots, record video, or load new plans unless you restart the system.
USB Not Valid

The system does not recognize the USB. Confirm that a compatible and formatted USB is used. The USB file system should be either FAT/FAT32 or NTFS. If the issue persists after confirming your USB's compatibility and formatting, use a different USB drive.

page_map.text: If the monitors time out when you plug in or unplug an external display or recording device from the System Cart, select Continue on the Controller touchscreen to synchronize the monitors, and then select Recover to resolve the issue.
A.21 System Faults
When a system fault occurs, the system displays a message on the monitor, the instrument arm locks, and the Catheter becomes inactive.

WARNING: When a system fault occurs, retract the tool inside the protective sheath immediately to minimize interaction with tissue and prevent patient injury as the Catheter slowly relaxes in response to the fault.
CAUTION: Failure to recognize and recover from system faults may result in procedure delay.
Non-Recoverable Fault

In the event of a non-recoverable fault, system LEDs illuminate red (if applicable). See A.2 Midprocedure Restart on page 94. If the fault persists, contact Customer Service to troubleshoot the issue.
Recoverable Fault

In the event of a recoverable fault, system LEDs illuminate yellow on the part of the system that needs attention to recover the fault (if applicable). Follow system messages to recover and continue with the procedure. Or, tap Recover Fault on the Controller touchscreen.
A.22 Patient Motion

The system detects if there is significant patient motion, and shows a notification on the top monitor. If patient motion is detected, evaluate registration accuracy by ensuring the Live View matches with the Navigation View while driving. Perform one of the following steps:
If registration is accurate, tap Dismiss.
If registration is not accurate, tap Redo Registration to perform registration again.

Note: Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube may be detected as patient motion, and result in a patient motion notification from the system. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter.
Battery Backup
Before starting a procedure, the system must be plugged in to mains power.

If the System Cart is unplugged from mains power during a procedure, the system alerts you that it is running on battery power and advises you to plug the System Cart into mains power to avoid loss of power.
If the system loses mains power during a procedure:
Troubleshooting | Mid-Procedure Catheter Exchange
D.7 Electromagnetic Compatibility

The Ion System with OnSite has been tested and found to be in compliance with IEC 60601-1-2, International standard for Medical electrical equipment -Part 1-2: General requirements for basic safety and essential performance -Collateral standard: Electromagnetic compatibility -Requirements and tests. It is intended to be used in a procedure room environment and operation of the system is unaffected when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in Tables 1-3 in this section. Special precautions and installation information for the system for Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) are provided in this section, see EMC Tables on page 111.

The performance of the system is unaffected when exposed to the electromagnetic environment as described in the IEC 60601-1-2 standard. There is no degradation of performance and therefore no risks to the patient or other devices due to Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) when used in the electromagnetic environment as specified in the tables in this section.

WARNING: Use of this equipment adjacent to or stacked with other equipment should be avoided because it could result in improper operation. If such use is necessary, this equipment and the other equipment should be observed to verify that they are operating normally.

WARNING: Use of accessories, transducers, and cables other than those specified or provided by the manufacturer of this equipment could result in increased electromagnetic emissions or decreased electromagnetic immunity of this equipment and result in improper operation.
Note: The Ion system was tested with shielded 3-meter composite video, S-video, SDI, DVI, HDMI, and Ethernet cables.
FCC Compliance

Note: This equipment has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class A digital device, pursuant to Part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference when the equipment is operated in a commercial environment. This equipment generates, uses, and can radiate radio frequency energy, and if not installed and used in accordance with the instruction manual, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. Operation of this equipment in a residential area is likely to cause harmful interference in which case the user will be required to correct the interference at his own expense.
CAUTION:

The Live View video signal from the Vision Probe may be susceptible to interference from devices that transmit in the frequency of 80-90 MHz. If excessive noise is seen in the Live View, reorient or relocate the system or the interfering equipment to increase the distance between the two pieces of equipment.
EMC Tables
The following tables contain the Manufacturer's declaration and additional information required by IEC 60601-1-2: 2014.
Table 1: IEC60601-1-2:2014, Manufacturer's Declaration -Electronic Emissions

4.1 Device Description
The Ion endoluminal system navigates a flexible Catheter within the lung to a planned path in order to sample a target. It is comprised of the following components, instruments, and accessories:
PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop

PlanPoint Software generates a plan of the patient's airways from an existing CT scan, and the Planning Laptop is a portable computer used with the PlanPoint Software. The CT scan images are uploaded to the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop and segmented by the software. After identifying the target, the user can add a path to the target. The user can modify or create additional targets and paths as needed. The patient plan is transferred from the Planning Laptop to the Controller and displayed on the System Cart monitors for navigational guidance during the procedure.

Protected Health Information and Personal Data: Patient and surgeon information, including names, birth dates, and imaging study dates, are fictitious. In compliance with the U.S. Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and its foreign counterparts, no actual protected health information or personal data is used in this manual.
For additional information on PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop use, see the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
Ion System Cart

The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) consists of the instrument arm (with carriage), setup joint, brakes, and monitors (top and bottom). The instrument arm (referred to as the arm) adjusts to move the Catheter through the airway. The monitors present navigational information such as live video (Live View) from the Vision Probe, Navigation View, and biopsy target information. Third-party video sources including bronchoscope, fluoroscope, and radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS)) can also be displayed on the monitors.
For further information on System Cart use, see 4.2 System Cart Use on page 33.
Ion Fully Articulating Catheter
1. Housing
2. Sensor port
3. Input discs
4. Electrical contacts
5. Shaft
6. Tool channel entrance
7. Tool channel exit (tip)

The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) has an approximately 3.5 mm outer diameter (at the tip), and a 2 mm tool channel that allows for insertion of compatible tools. It is compatible with the Vision Probe, Flexision biopsy needles, and third-party tools. The fiber optic shape sensor in the Catheter provides the shape and position of the Catheter on the System Cart monitors. The Catheter has an articulating tip.
The Catheter consists of the housing, sensor, input discs, shaft, tool channel, and tip.

Appendix A Troubleshooting
This chapter explains troubleshooting and emergency scenarios:
A.9 Catheter Guide Attachment Errors
If the Catheter Guide is not detected or fails to install, refer to the specific troubleshooting guidance on the system.
If the issue persists after following the system's troubleshooting guidance, you may try the following to recover from the fault:
1. Disconnect and reinstall the Catheter Guide onto the arm. Ensure that the Catheter Guide is fully attached to the arm.
If the issue persists, proceed to Steps 2-4.
2. Disconnect the Catheter Guide from the arm.
3. Clean the Catheter Guide and System arm electrical contacts with an alcohol wipe or dry gauze.
4. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
If the issue persists, proceed to Steps 5-8.
5. Disconnect the Catheter Guide from the arm.
6. Restart the system.
7. Follow the on-screen prompts to complete the system tests.
8. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
If the issue persists, proceed to Step 9.
9. Install a new Catheter Guide onto the arm.
A.10 Catheter Tests Fail
If Catheter tests fail, refer to the specific troubleshooting guidance on the system.
To clean the sensor connections on the Catheter and the arm carriage:
1. Check that your Sensor Connection Cleaner has sufficient thread and is functioning properly. Replace the Sensor Connection Cleaner if you observe any of the following:
· Only red spool is visible in the window on the side of the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
· You feel resistance when pushing the handle to the point that the Sensor Connection Cleaner audibly clicks.
· The Sensor Connection Cleaner is not clicking properly.
2. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
4. Reinstall the Catheter.
· Repeat cleaning the sensor connections up to two times.
· Reinstall the Catheter Guide:
1. Disconnect the Catheter and Catheter Guide from the arm.
2. Reinstall the Catheter Guide.
· Restart the system:
1. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
2. Restart the system, then follow the on-screen prompts to complete the system tests.
· Replace the Catheter:
2. Obtain a new Catheter.
3. Clean the sensor connections on both the new Catheter and the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
4. Install the new Catheter.
A.11 Catheter Not Moving (Controls Unresponsive)
If the Catheter is not moving or the trackball or scroll wheel is not responding, ensure that the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are securely connected to the docking spar.

If the Catheter Guide and Swivel Connector are connected to the docking spar, remove the trackball or scroll wheel from its cup, reinstall, and wait for calibration. Clean the trackball or scroll wheel if necessary, and ensure that both are reinstalled fully into their cups.
If the issue persists, try any of the following:
· Clean the Catheter Guide connections.
· Install a new Catheter Guide.

page_map.section_title: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
page_map.text: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)

page_map.section_title: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
page_map.text: When inserting the Vision Probe through the Catheter, the system will detect the color stripes inside the Catheter to ensure vision is oriented correctly while driving.

page_map.section_title: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
page_map.text: If the stripes are not visible, a message appears when the Vision Probe reaches the Catheter tip. The message indicates that orientation was not accurately detected and instructs you to partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter. Always make sure the Vision Probe tip is clean.

page_map.section_title: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
page_map.text: If the system does not present the message because it did not detect the stripes (or if it detects the stripes incorrectly), the Vision Probe image will appear to be 90 or 180 degrees rotated, and driving will be non-intuitive. In this case, partially retract the Vision Probe until the stripes inside the Catheter are clearly visible, and then reinsert the Vision Probe through the Catheter.

page_map.section_title: A.12 Rotated Vision Probe View (Non-intuitive Driving)
page_map.text: If the issue persists, try replacing the Vision Probe, the Catheter, or both.

page_map.section_title: A.13 Live View Displays Colored Lines
page_map.text: A.13 Live View Displays Colored Lines

page_map.section_title: A.13 Live View Displays Colored Lines
page_map.text: If the Live View (Vision Probe view) on the bottom monitor displays colored lines, install a new Vision Probe onto the system and ensure that the leak test port remains closed. Check the leak test port of the old Vision Probe for fluid or condensation. If no fluid is present, the Vision Probe may have been damaged due to a tight turn or bend radius.
A.14 Vision Probe Image Quality
If the Vision Probe image is not clear, try the following:
· Inject 0.5 to 2 mL of air or saline into the Catheter tool channel and aspirate back as needed to clear any bubbles.
· Clean the tip of the Vision Probe with isopropyl alcohol.

If the Catheter is retracted into the ET tube, you can remove the Catheter from the ET tube and wipe the tip of the Catheter and Vision Probe together. Otherwise, remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter, wipe the Vision Probe tip, and re-insert the Vision Probe.
· If there are secretions within the Catheter tool channel,
1. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
2. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter.
3. Place the Catheter tip into a bowl of saline.
4. Place the Suction Adapter onto the Catheter tool channel and apply suction.
5. Dry the Catheter by suctioning air through the tool channel.
6. Ensure the Vision Probe is clean and re-insert it into the Catheter.
A.15 Vision Probe Not Detected

If the system does not detect the Vision Probe, remove the Vision Probe and reinstall it. If the issue persists, remove the Vision Probe and install a new Vision Probe. If the Vision Probe is still not detected, restart the system.
A.16 Live View Not Advancing
If the Live View is not advancing or the Swivel Connector disconnects repeatedly, try the following to resolve the issue:
· Adjust the elevation angle of the arm to allow for Swivel Connector connection.
· Re-lubricate the Catheter to reduce tension.
· Monitor drive force during navigation. Elevated drive force may indicate that the Swivel Connector is susceptible to disconnecting from the arm.
A.17 Swivel Connector Disconnects
If the Swivel Connector disconnects repeatedly or the Live View is not advancing, try the following to resolve the issue:

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: If the top monitor displays a grey spinning wheel during navigation, there is an interruption in the Catheter sensor connection due to a tight bend radius (tight turn in the Catheter tip).

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: To resolve the issue:

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: 1. If needed, mark the original Catheter position with a biopsy marker.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: 2. Straighten the Catheter using any of the following methods:

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: · Articulate the trackball in the direction of the white arrow that is displayed on the tip indicator.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: · Slightly retract the Catheter.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: If the issue persists, the following may improve tight turn navigation:

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: · Re-lubricate the Catheter.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: · Undock and retract the ET tube (which requires re-registering). This gives the Catheter more length beyond the tip of the ET tube, which allows the Catheter to build more support against the trachea wall to make a wider turn.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: Under fluoroscopy, monitor the Catheter and look for a delay in Catheter advancement as indication that you are building support against the trachea wall.

page_map.section_title: A.18 Spinning Wheel on Monitor (Catheter Shape Sensor Interference)
page_map.text: · Use the carriage clutch button to retract the carriage and release tension.
A.19 Touchscreen Unresponsive

If the Controller touchscreen is unresponsive, the system may detect fluid on the screen. Wipe any visible fluid from the screen and wait five seconds before attempting to make a selection. Otherwise, wait five seconds before making a selection.
If the issue persists, restart the system.
A.23 Mid-Procedure Catheter Exchange
2. Retract the Catheter into the ET tube using the scroll wheel or carriage clutch button.
3. Retract the Catheter Guide.
4. Pull the Catheter out of the ET tube to remove the Catheter from the patient.
5. Remove Vision Probe from the Catheter, but keep it connected to the arm.
6. Disconnect the Catheter from the arm.
7. Tap Continue Procedure on the Controller touchscreen.
8. Raise the arm carriage, if needed.
9. Get a new Catheter, and then clean the sensor connections on the new Catheter and on the arm carriage using the Sensor Connection Cleaner (see Step 2 on page 60 and Step 3 on page 61).
10. Install the new Catheter and allow the Catheter self-tests to complete.
11. Insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter tool channel.
12. Lubricate the Catheter, and insert the Catheter into the ET tube.
13. Extend the Catheter Guide, and advance the Catheter.
14. Perform registration.
Check Connections
In case of inconsistent power behavior, first check AC power connections:
1. Confirm the power cable is properly connected to a dedicated AC power outlet.
2. Confirm the power breaker switch is On (indicated by an 'I' near the switch). The power breaker switch is on the back of the System Cart.

The Ion system has a design life of five years; however, even after five years, the standard maintenance contract provides for preventive maintenance, inspection and re-qualification by qualified Intuitive personnel that extends the service life of the system until the next scheduled service.

ifu.device_name: System, Instruments, and Accessories User Manual
intended_use: The Ion System Cart (referred to as the System Cart) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.
The Ion Controller (referred to as the Controller) is intended to facilitate navigation and positioning of endoscopic instruments in the pulmonary tract.

The Ion Fully Articulating Catheter (referred to as the Catheter) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system for navigating to the target region in the airways. It is intended to also provide a conduit for the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe, Flexision Biopsy Needles and delivering compatible off-the-shelf tools.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is intended to retrieve tissue from a target structure.
The Ion Peripheral Vision Probe (referred to as the Vision Probe) is intended to be used with the Ion endoluminal system to provide live airway view for catheter navigation.
The Vision Probe Adapter is intended to be used to connect the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Vision Probe Bag is used for temporary storage of the Ion Peripheral Vision Probe during a procedure.
The Catheter Guide is intended to be used with the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to provide support.
The Sensor Connection Cleaner is used for cleaning the sensor connections on the carriage of the Ion System Cart and the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
The Swivel Connector is intended to be used to connect the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter to an endotracheal tube.
The Suction Adapter is intended to allow modulation of suction when suction tubing is connected to the Ion Fully Articulating Catheter.
Only physicians with adequate training and experience in bronchoscopic techniques and adequate healthcare facilities should perform procedures with the Ion endoluminal system.

Training provided by Intuitive is limited to the use of the Ion endoluminal system and does not replace the necessary medical training and experience required to perform diagnostic and therapeutic bronchoscopy procedures.
indications_for_use: The Ion endoluminal system (Model IF1000), referred to in this manual as "the system," assists the user in navigating a catheter and endoscopic tools in the pulmonary tract using endoscopic visualization of the tracheobronchial tree for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The Ion endoluminal system enables fiducial marker placement. It does not make a diagnosis and is not for pediatric use.
The PlanPoint Software uses patient CT scans to create a 3D plan of the lung and navigation pathways for use with the Ion endoluminal system.
The Flexision Biopsy Needle is used with the Ion endoluminal system to biopsy tissue from a target area in the lung.

setup_steps.text: Remove the Catheter Reprocessing Cover from the Catheter:
Inspect the Catheter Reprocessing Cover for any fluid, especially in the well that protects the green sensor port.
If not already done, move the System Cart to the desired location and apply the brakes.
Follow instructions in Chapter 5 Room Setup on page 48.
Position the patient on the procedure table (bed).

procedure_steps.text: Needle stroke length markings
If not already done, move the System Cart to the desired location and apply the brakes.
Follow instructions in Chapter 5 Room Setup on page 48.
To repeat biopsy, insert the needle and repeat the needle biopsy steps to perform another biopsy pass from the same target to collect an appropriate sample size, at the physician's discretion.
Perform biopsy passes.
Remove samples from the needle (see Remove Samples on page 82).
Navigate to a second target (if applicable).
Repeat Navigation and Biopsy steps of the procedure.
If a biopsy tool (for example, needle, forceps, or brush) is advanced through the Catheter tool channel, retract the biopsy tool into its protective sheath and remove it from the Catheter.

Keep the Catheter attached to the arm (the Catheter shaft may remain inside the patient). If the Catheter is removed from the arm, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
Keep the system docked to the patient. If the system is undocked, you will need to complete Guided Setup and re-register after the system restarts.
Position the patient on the procedure table (bed).
Dock the arm to the Swivel Connector.
(Optional) Perform a radial endobronchial ultrasound (R-Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS)) using fluoroscopy to confirm the target location.
Position the Catheter for biopsy.
Insert the biopsy needle through the Catheter tool channel. Secure the needle to the Catheter.

enrichment.title: First Experience of Personalized in Situ Tissue Engineering for Thoracic Surgery of the Sarcoma Patient: MSCs-Containing Minimally Manipulated Cells and an Individualized Micropore Titanium Sternum in a One-Year Follow-Up Case Report.
enrichment.journal: International journal of hematology-oncology and stem cell research
enrichment.abstract: Individually customized grafts have become standard for reconstructing extensive chest wall defects resulting from surgical interventions for sternal malignant neoplasms. However, the outcomes of these graft implantations can be further improved by administering patient-derived cells, which have minimal oncological risks. In 2021, a 52-year-old woman with chondrosarcoma (pT2N0M0G2, stage IIB) was admitted to the Department of Thoracic Surgery. The patient presented with a large tumor in the body of the sternum, measuring 81 × 94 × 91 mm, according to the computed tomography (CT) scan. To address this, an individualized endoprosthesis was modeled and created using the original 'pincer-dock' construction based on CT-scan screens. The mononuclear cell fraction (MNCs) was obtained from the patient's peripheral blood one week before surgery using a Haemonetics cell separation device and cryopreserved until the day of the procedure. The resulting 30 mL MNC suspension contained 12 mln cells per 1 mL. We performed flow cytometry analysis using a FACS Aria III flow cytometer to confirm the presence of mesenchymal stromal cells in the MNCs. We also performed immunostaining for S-100, a common tumor marker for benign and malignant diseases, and D2-40, a marker for the lymphatic endothelium that reacts with Kaposi's sarcoma and a subset of angiosarcomas. None of the cells were positive for either marker. Approximately 3 ml of the MNC suspension was injected into each rib edge and 30 ml into the operating field immediately after resection. The titanium endoprosthesis was placed in the sternal defect, and the body of the endoprosthesis was securely covered with a laparoscopically mobilized omental flap. After a one-year follow-up, the patient showed no signs of recurrence or post-surgical complications. These outstanding functional and cosmetic results highlight the potential for the broader clinical utilization of minimally manipulated cells in personalized medicine in oncology. These results could pave the way for wider clinical application of peripheral blood-derived minimally manipulated cells in personalized medicine as an adjuvant for titanium endoprosthesis reconstruction of osteochondral defects in patients with sarcoma.

enrichment.title: Superior capsule reconstruction stabilizes the humeral head during scaption: in vivo 3-dimensional kinematic analysis using model-image registration.
enrichment.abstract: It has been proven that superior capsule reconstruction (SCR) improves the superior translation of the humeral head through cadaveric studies. However, there has been limited information on in vivo glenohumeral kinematics of shoulders with SCR. The purpose of this study was to compare pre- and postoperative glenohumeral kinematics in shoulders that underwent arthroscopic SCR using model-image registration techniques.

table_cells.text: Tap to preview the Navigation View in either Lock to Path or Preview Path mode, with the option to view any vasculature that was added during planning. Note the various preview modes and options: • Lock to Path mode: On by default, Lock to Path locks the Navi- gation View to the path towards the selected destination. Lock to Path mode forces the Navigation View to remain on the path to the target, but still follows the insertion motion of the real Catheter, and can be used with the Live View to accurately facil- itate navigation to the target. While relying on the Live View, use Lock to Path to indicate which turns to make. If there is divergence between the Live View and Navigation View, use the arrows that appear on the touchscreen to adjust the insertion or retraction of the Navigation View to match the Live View. Use the Move Target or Catheter reference function- ality to help localize the target. • Preview Path mode: Tap Scroll Wheel Lock to unlock Lock to Path and enter Preview Path to preview the selected path to the target without moving the actual Catheter. Use the arrows to move the Navigation View Catheter forward or backward through the airway. See Figure 4.22. • Vasculature: Depicts both arteries and veins in red. Tap Vascu- lature to toggle the visibility of any vasculature that was added during planning. Vasculature is visible only in the Navigation View when either Preview Path or Lock to Path mode is active.

Tap and hold with one finger to rotate, tap and hold with two fingers to pan, and pinch to zoom into the airway tree on the monitor. The Tree View is set to follow Catheter movement by default and stops when the tree is rotated. Recenter to follow the Catheter movement again. The Tree View can be rotated only in manual view. You can also toggle the visibility of the target, reference areas, and anatomy borders. • Airway Tree: Tap Airway Tree to view the approximate shape of the Catheter within the airways. If the target is updated, the option to switch to Airway Tree is disabled until the target is reset. • Set the angle for Tree View to match the fluoroscope angle, or input any desired angle by tapping Adjust Angle on the Con- troller touchscreen. Rotate the Tree View to get the optimal angle for viewing by tapping the view orientations on the Con- troller touchscreen (Axial, Sagittal, Coronal, Follow, Manual, and Adjust Angle). Tap Coronal to rotate the tree to the anterior- posterior view.

Drive with caution in small airways where the airway diameter is smaller than the outer diameter of the Catheter.

If friction is felt in the trackball or scroll wheel, clean it with saline and dry with gauze prior to or during use, as needed.
Calibration initiates after installing the trackball and scroll wheel. Do not touch the trackball or scroll wheel during calibration. The Controller has the following components:

Once the target is moved, the Airway Tree and anatomy borders are no longer visible on the Top Monitor since the Catheter-to-target relationship has been updated. To restore the airway tree and anatomy borders, undo the updated target, tap Adjust Tree in the quick tools bar, and tap Airway Tree.
Do not remove the USB while recording or immediately after stopping recording, as this may result in corrupt video files.
Do not block access to the primary electrical plug (or main disconnect from supply). Ensure there is clearance in the room for the primary electrical plug for the system.

Before clinical use, always inspect the system and Controller for any damage (for example, broken, cracked, chipped, or worn parts). If you observe any damage, contact Customer Service and do not use the system.
If the system does not power on as expected, restart the system.
Endotracheal tube is required to perform the procedure.
During a procedure, have backup instruments and accessories available that are required to perform an Ion procedure in case of instrument failure.
. Release the lever to unlock the Catheter Reprocessing Cover.
. Firmly grasp and lift the strap, and then move the strap to the open position.
. Remove the Catheter from the Catheter Reprocessing Cover.
Check compatibility of third-party tools prior to use.

Whenever you connect the Catheter to the system, clean the sensor connections on the arm carriage and on the Catheter itself using the Sensor Connection Cleaner. This includes the first time you attach the Catheter to the system, as well as any time you reattach or replace the Catheter on the system.
Ensure the Vision Probe is not twisted during insertion to prevent image flipping.

If the Vision Probe Bag is not used for temporary storage of the Vision Probe when it is not inserted within the Catheter tool channel, it is recommended to use an alternate, legally marketed, method to store the Vision Probe during the procedure.
. Retrieve the Sensor Connection Cleaner from its storage location.
. Check the window on the side of the Sensor Connection Cleaner to ensure that there is white thread remaining. If the window is fully red, get a replacement Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Push the handle of the Sensor Connection Cleaner until it audibly clicks. If you feel resistance or if the cleaner is not functioning properly, replace the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Remove the gray cap from the inside of the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Insert the Sensor Connection Cleaner into the arm carriage sensor port. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
. Push the handle until it audibly clicks. Repeat three times.
. Remove the adapter from the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Hold the Catheter such that the sensor port is visible.
. Insert the narrow end of the Sensor Connection Cleaner into the Catheter sensor port, to open the shutter.

. Ensure the tip of the Sensor Connection Cleaner is inserted into the sensor connection (small round hole) inside the Catheter sensor port. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
. Thread the Catheter shaft through the compressed Catheter Guide. Connect the Catheter onto the arm carriage.
. Ensure the Catheter tip has room to perform self-tests. Wait for the Catheter tests to finish.
. Thread the Vision Probe Adapter onto the Vision Probe.
. Twist the adapter onto the Vision Probe. Gently pull to ensure connection is secure.
. Place the Vision Probe in a clean place.
. Open the bag by pulling out the bottom tab.
. Unfold the strap and slide it down, over the arm.
. Adjust the bag opening as needed to allow smooth insertion of the Vision Probe to store it when not in use during the procedure. Do not kink the Vision Probe while inserting it into the bag.
. Place the Catheter on a clean surface.
Information for the patient plan selection includes patient name, medical record number (MRN), and plan date.

Before you can access plans on the Network Drive, you must complete a one-time linking process between your Intuitive account and your local PlanPoint account. For instructions on linking your accounts, see the PlanPoint Software and Planning Laptop Supplement.
If you load a plan from the Network Drive, a USB device is still required to collect screenshots and video recording during a procedure.
. Ensure you have logged in to your Intuitive account (see 8.5 Log in to Your Intuitive Account on page 67).
. Enter your six-digit Intuitive PIN to authenticate your account.
If you cannot access the Network Drive, load the patient plan onto the system using a USB device and contact Customer Service.
. Ensure you have logged in to your Intuitive account if you wish to collect real-time case data associated with your procedure (see 8.5 Log in to Your Intuitive Account on page 67).
. If prompted for your PIN, you may tap Skip on the PIN pad to bypass authentication. Authentication is required only to access patient plans on the Network Drive.
. Insert the USB device with the exported plan into the USB input on the Controller.
If you are loading the plan from the Network Drive and the plan is not available, load the plan onto the system using a USB device.
Navigation View should be used as guidance only.
. Before use of the needle, confirm the label is legible and is the intended needle size.
. Before use and between each use, inspect the needle for the following:

. Before inserting or reinserting into the Catheter tool channel, confirm the needle is fully retracted and locked within the sheath, the needle sheath home position mark is fully exposed, and the thumbscrew has locked the sheath extension. WARNING: Confirm the relation of the patient anatomy to the biopsy target (for example, distances to target and anatomy borders) before setting needle stroke length. Setting the incorrect needle stroke length may lead to pneumothorax.
Select a vacuum locking syringe and stopcock with standard luer lock connectors (luer fittings compliant with ISO 80369-7) that can suction up to 20 mL.
. Set the needle insertion limit.
. With the sheath pointing towards the sample tray, advance the needle.
. Push the sample out using a syringe filled with air.
. Retract the needle and secure the needle stop.
. Reinsert the stylet into the needle and lock in place. Ensure the needle is not damaged (for example, bent or broken).
. Ensure that the Catheter bend radius is greater than 25 mm if inserting forceps or greater than 20 mm if inserting any other third-party tools.
. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.
. Ensure the forceps are fully closed.

Slowly insert and retract biopsy forceps through the Catheter tool channel. Quickly inserting and retracting may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
. Gently rotate the forceps back and forth while retracting until the resistance is overcome. If resistance persists, or the tool is jammed, remove the Catheter and biopsy tool together.
When possible before performing lavage, it is recommended to retract the Catheter so it is away from the airway walls for free fluid flow.
Do not manually force the carriage to move unless necessary. Use carriage clutch button or scroll wheel to safely move the carriage.
Do not store the system in a temperature below -20 ºC or higher than 60 ºC. Exposure to temperature outside the range -20 ºC to 60 °C may damage the product.
. Room temperature between 50 to 86 °F (10 to 30 °C).
. Relative humidity between 10 to 85% non-condensing.
Do not unlock the System Cart brakes or move the arm (setup joint) while the system restarts, or else you will be prompted to re-register after completing Guided Setup.
If the biopsy needle or a biopsy tool is advanced into the tissue through the Catheter tool channel, then pull the needle back into its protecting sheath and into the Catheter before pressing E-stop.
You will need to register 4 cm on each side of the main carina to complete registration.

If a plan has already been loaded when you get this error, you may continue with the loaded plan, but note that you cannot take screenshots, record video, or load new plans unless you restart the system.
After performing the troubleshooting steps below, if only one monitor returns to a live feed, perform a mid-procedure restart to resolve the issue. See A.2 Mid-procedure Restart on page 94.

Catheter buckling or excessive friction in the ET tube may be detected as patient motion, and result in a patient motion notification from the system. Ensure sufficient lubrication is applied to the Catheter.
The Ion system was tested with shielded 3-meter composite video, S-video, SDI, DVI, HDMI, and Ethernet cables.

This equipment has been tested and found to comply with the limits for a Class A digital device, pursuant to Part 15 of the FCC Rules. These limits are designed to provide reasonable protection against harmful interference when the equipment is operated in a commercial environment. This equipment generates, uses, and can radiate radio frequency energy, and if not installed and used in accordance with the instruction manual, may cause harmful interference to radio communications. Operation of this equipment in a residential area is likely to cause harmful interference in which case the user will be required to correct the interference at his own expense.
UT is the AC mains voltage before application of the test level.

The Ion system, instruments, and accessories are not intended specifically to control, diagnose, monitor, or correct a defect of the heart, central circulatory, or central nervous system through direct contact with those parts of the body.
. Automatically configured video format supports 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x720, 1280x1024, and 1920x1080. Not all DVI receiving devices support automatic configuration.
. Frame rate is determined by country.
. SDI interlaced video signals are not supported.
If Controller responsiveness is poor, change or dry gloves. The Controller touchscreen and scroll wheel are designed to sense touch. Wet gloves may interfere with touch sensing.

number (MRN), and plan date.
. Keep the arm in a close-to-vertical position while docking. This allows for gradual bends in the ET tube.
. Use the arm clutch and powered elevation buttons to position the arm so that the angle of the docking spar aligns with the angle of the Swivel Connector and docks with minimal bends in the ET tube.

. Stabilize the ET tube and Swivel Connector with one hand (with help from the anesthesiologist, as needed), and use the other hand to press and hold the arm clutch button to bring the instrument arm magnetic mount to the Swivel Connector.
. Dock the arm at a close-to-perpendicular angle to the ET tube.
Once docked to the Swivel Connector, the arm clutch button activates after holding it for approximately two seconds.
. Tap Confirm Main Carina on the Controller touchscreen.
. Position the Catheter for R-Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) approximately 10 mm proximal to the lesion.
. Adjust the fluoroscope to match the optimal fluoro angle on the top monitor.
. Perform R-Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS). If needed, use Fluoro Reference and Articulation Guide with R-Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) to localize the target (see Biopsy Tab on page 41).
. If needed, select Move Target to update the target position (see Biopsy Tab on page 41).
. Re-insert the Vision Probe into the Catheter.
. Look for tenting under fluoroscopy (indicated by backward movement of the Catheter).
. Confirm that the Catheter and sheath are aligned to the target.
. After placement of the sheath tip, tighten the thumbscrew to lock the sheath position.
Do not advance forceps through the Catheter tool channel if the bend radius is smaller than 25 mm. Do not advance any other third-party tools if the bend radius is smaller than 20 mm.
. Retract the Catheter into the ET tube.
. Retract the Catheter Guide and remove the Catheter from the ET tube.
. Remove the Vision Probe from the Catheter and uninstall the Vision Probe connector from the arm by rotating and pulling the collar.
. Remove the Vision Probe Bag by sliding the strap up and over the arm after the Vision Probe has been disconnected.
. Remove the Catheter from the arm using the Catheter release buttons on the arm.
. Install the Catheter Reprocessing Cover onto the Catheter (refer to the Ion Instruments Reprocessing Instructions).
. Remove the trackball and the scroll wheel from Controller.

. Using quaternary ammonium based cleaner disinfectant disposable wipes, follow the wipe manufacturer's instructions to clean and disinfect the trackball, scroll wheel, magnet, and Controller. Roll the scroll wheel to ensure coverage. Ensure the trackball and scroll wheel cups are wiped.
. After drying, re-insert the trackball and scroll wheel into the Controller.
. Ensure all accessories have been removed, and extend the arm fully using the carriage clutch button.
. Place reusable accessories aside for cleaning. See the Reprocessing Instructions User Manual for further information.
. Dispose singleuse accessories following all applicable national and local laws and guidelines.
. Using quaternary ammonium based cleaner disinfectant disposable wipes, follow the wipe manufacturer's instructions to clean and disinfect the arm.
Storage and transport of the system are not affected by atmospheric pressure.

The emissions characteristics of this equipment make it suitable for use in industrial areas and hospitals (CISPR 11 class A). If it is used in a residential environment (for which CISPR 11 class B is normally required) this equipment might not offer adequate protection to radio-frequency communication services. The user might need to take mitigation measures, such as relocating or re-orienting the equipment.
Transient flicker, color bars, or fault messages related to loss of image are acceptable.

. Retrieve the Sensor Connection Cleaner from its storage location.
. Check the window on the side of the Sensor Connection Cleaner to ensure that there is white thread remaining. If the window is fully red, get a replacement Sensor Connection Cleaner.

. Place the Catheter on a clean surface.

. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.

. Retrieve the Sensor Connection Cleaner from its storage location.
. Check the window on the side of the Sensor Connection Cleaner to ensure that there is white thread remaining. If the window is fully red, get a replacement Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Push the handle of the Sensor Connection Cleaner until it audibly clicks. If you feel resistance or if the cleaner is not functioning properly, replace the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Remove the gray cap from the inside of the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Insert the Sensor Connection Cleaner into the arm carriage sensor port. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
. Push the handle until it audibly clicks. Repeat three times.
. Remove the adapter from the Sensor Connection Cleaner.
. Hold the Catheter such that the sensor port is visible.
. Insert the narrow end of the Sensor Connection Cleaner into the Catheter sensor port, to open the shutter.

. Ensure the tip of the Sensor Connection Cleaner is inserted into the sensor connection (small round hole) inside the Catheter sensor port. Ensure that the Sensor Connection Cleaner is straight when inserted.
. Thread the Catheter shaft through the compressed Catheter Guide. Connect the Catheter onto the arm carriage.
. Ensure the Catheter tip has room to perform self-tests. Wait for the Catheter tests to finish.
. Thread the Vision Probe Adapter onto the Vision Probe.
. Twist the adapter onto the Vision Probe. Gently pull to ensure connection is secure.
. Place the Vision Probe in a clean place.
. Open the bag by pulling out the bottom tab.
. Unfold the strap and slide it down, over the arm.
. Adjust the bag opening as needed to allow smooth insertion of the Vision Probe to store it when not in use during the procedure. Do not kink the Vision Probe while inserting it into the bag.
. Place the Catheter on a clean surface.

. Set the needle insertion limit.
. With the sheath pointing towards the sample tray, advance the needle.
. Push the sample out using a syringe filled with air.
. Retract the needle and secure the needle stop.
. Reinsert the stylet into the needle and lock in place. Ensure the needle is not damaged (for example, bent or broken).
. Ensure that the Catheter bend radius is greater than 25 mm if inserting forceps or greater than 20 mm if inserting any other third-party tools.
. Once the device is inserted, the Catheter can be articulated to achieve a tighter bend radius, if needed.
. Ensure the forceps are fully closed.

Slowly insert and retract biopsy forceps through the Catheter tool channel. Quickly inserting and retracting may result in Catheter sensor interference. When interference is detected, the system transitions the Catheter to passive state. Recover on the Controller touchscreen and reposition the Catheter as needed.
. Gently rotate the forceps back and forth while retracting until the resistance is overcome. If resistance persists, or the tool is jammed, remove the Catheter and biopsy tool together.

Do not manually force the carriage to move unless necessary. Use carriage clutch button or scroll wheel to safely move the carriage.
